newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Yankee sets up decommissioning group.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Yankee sets up decommissioning group.

text.p: Connecticut Yankee Atomic Power Plant said Tuesday it is setting up a community group to advise on the decommissioning of the plant.
The committee will hold its first meeting sometime in March.
Connecticut Yankee is operated and 49-percent owned by Northeast Utilities.
A group of power companies headed by Northeast said in December 1996 they would permanently close the Connecticut Yankee station, one of the nation's oldest nuclear plants.
The 582-megawatt plant had been shut down for repairs and refueling since July of last year.
Northeast has said the dismantling will cost about $425 million.

Citizens' watchdog groups say they are concerned that neither the utility nor the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission are doing enough to safeguard the public against the hazards posed by decommissioning.
They argue that the spent fuel poses a significant danger to the public.
The new committee will be chaired by retired State Senator Kenneth Hampton, according to Connecticut Yankee.

"We are seeking a broad representation to address public questions and concerns as they relate to the decommissioning of the CY nuclear power plant," Hampton said in the statement issued by Connecticut Yankee.
The Community Decommissioning Advisory Committee will have 17 members appointed by their town or sponsoring agency.
"The committee effectively sets in place a means of formally maintaining a dialogue between the greater CY community and the soon to be decommissioned plant," Connecticut Yankee said.
